sentence: Nevertheles I wold wishe that beside them, hereafter, whan time shal serve, the superflous and tediouse statutes were brought into one summe together, and made more plaine and short, to th’intent that men might the better understaund them, wich thing shal moch help to avaunce the profit of the commonweale.
source: J. G. Nichols (ed.), Literary Remains of King Edward the Sixth, vol. 2 (London: Roxburghe Club, 1857), p. 486, 'Discourse on the Reformation of Abuses, 1551', section 2, 'Devising of good lawes'
